blocker.location: 240/0, right exit chokepoint, on-screen stop position (44,12)
observations: 3 methodologically distinct approaches (raw Navigator.move! taps; Navigator.avoid_hostiles_and_push! default radius=16; avoid_hostiles_and_push! radius=32; avoid_hostiles_and_push! via a down-then-right alternate route) all converge on the EXACT same on-screen stop position (44,12) and the exact same HP floor (8/24 from a 24/24 start) -- technique-independent convergence, not a controller-skill gap.

2 OAM-confirmed tile=0x50 object pairs sit just past the chokepoint (screen x=70,y=30 and further east) -- static, non-mobile, 4-frame idle animation, never yet reached for a face+:a interaction test.

Room genuinely SCROLLS past this point (SCY shift observed, single tap moved y from 36 to 12) -- the chokepoint sits right around the scroll boundary, a plausible reason a fixed-radius avoidance primitive underperforms here specifically.
known_constraints: D12: no RAM writes to bypass the obstacle (0xDB5A must never be written)
no weapon/A-slot item confirmed owned yet
owner explicitly declined a D12 HP-write exception for this specific blocker and asked for a genuinely different approach instead

hypotheses.statement: The chokepoint is passable without any HP-floor regression below the already-established 8/24 by reading hostile OAM positions live each step and only advancing right when no hostile is within contact range (an opportunistic gap-dash), because the hostiles wander/patrol (documented elsewhere in this project) rather than permanently occupying the chokepoint -- a fixed-radius avoidance primitive (tested at radius 16 and 32) cannot exploit a moving gap the way a live polling loop can.

The chokepoint is a genuine structural gate: hostile patrol paths permanently overlap this exact screen position with no exploitable timing gap, so even an opportunistic gap-dash will still take unavoidable contact converging on the same (44,12)/8-24-HP signature already seen 3 times -- passing legitimately requires an item not yet found (a weapon or equivalent), not a better technique.

The 240/0 chokepoint damage is not purely from the wandering tile=0x6a/0x68 hostile: the 2 static tile=0x50 round objects near it (never contact-tested, closest approach only 25-30px) may be a variant of the oursin/sea-urchin hazard family already documented at riverside_flower_clearing (225/0, tile=0x5C/0x5E) -- a STATIC contact-damage hazard, not an active attacker. The signpost there explicitly says a shield protects against oursins specifically (dialogues.riverside_flower_clearing_sign, page 2: "Se proteger avec un bouclier!"), a claim never actually tested in-game (registry note: shield was only ever measured as partial knockback-mitigation against the WANDERING 0x60-family, never as a full block against a static oursin-type object). If true, deliberately walking into contact with a tile=0x50 object while shield-equipped (B held, facing it) should show ZERO HP cost on that specific contact, unlike contact with the wandering 0x6a/0x68 creature, which the D13 primitive already showed still costs HP even while shielded.
